Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 4. децембар ст. ст., „Свети Јован Дамаскин.“ — with only «Свети» left off, that being “saint” and not a rank. «Дамаскин» is the by-name of his city and not a rank, it is the whole of what tells him from the eleven folders that share a bare «јован», and §6 asks for the fullest form the calendar gives. `sr-foldpred.mjs` measured the folded string at 0 other holders.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 4 decembrie — «Sfântul Cuvios Ioan Damaschin»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 4ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Όσιος Ιωάννης ο Δαμασκηνός»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 4 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the page, and it is the same man: its heading reads «(; - 749)» and it names Damascus, his father Sergios, the monastery of Saint Sabbas and the three orations for the holy icons. Of the page's hymns the first Ἀπολυτίκιον and the Κοντάκιον, both of which name him, are taken here; the «Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον», the Μεγαλυνάριον and the Κάθισμα are not drafted. Its long catalogue of his writings was read and is reported in summary rather than copied.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 17.12.2025 (4. децембар ст. ст.) — „Свети Јован Дамаскин.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, quoted whole with its closing full stop; URL year 2025. `types` UNTOUCHED: `venerable`, `monk`, `presbyter`, `hymnographer` and `theologian` are all already held, and «први министар калифа» is an office of state and no rank in BRIEF-SERBIAN §5’s table. NO `office` ADDED: the four locale packs would each owe a word for the caliph’s first minister and a reader should not invent four, so the ministry is in the life only. `dates` WIDENED on the death from a flat 749 to 749–776 — TWO BOOKS TWENTY-SEVEN YEARS APART. saint.gr says «κοιμήθηκε ειρηνικά το 749 μ.Χ.» and heads him «(; - 749)»; this book closes «Упокојио се мирно око 776. године у стотину четвртој години свога живота», he reposed in peace about 776 in the hundred and fourth year of his life. Nothing is chosen and the basis stays traditional. `birth` UNTOUCHED AND NOT RECOMPUTED: a hundred and four years back from 776 is a year this book does not print, and BRIEF.md §5 keeps an inferred year out of the file; the age is in the life and in this note instead. NO `locations`, and the folder has never held one — which also keeps `map-span.test.mjs` out of it, the widened death and the open birth now reading as a hundred and one years. NO `related` ROW ADDED: the monastery of Saint Sabbas is a dedication and BRIEF.md §4 says a dedication is not a relation; the caliph Abdalmelech and the emperor Leo the Isaurian are no folders this corpus holds. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Îndreptătorule al Ortodoxiei, învăţătorule al dreptei cinstiri de Dumnezeu şi al curăţiei şi luminătorule al lumii, podoaba călugărilor cea de Dumnezeu insuflată Sfinte Părinte Ioan, înţelepte, cu învăţăturile tale pe toţi i-ai luminat. Alăută duhovnicească, roagă-te lui Hristos Dumnezeu ca să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Ioan Damaschin

english.text: Guide of Orthodoxy, teacher of the right worship of God and of purity, light of the world, God-inspired adornment of monks, wise father John: by your teachings you have enlightened all. Spiritual harp, pray to Christ God that our souls be saved.

hymns.text: Τὴν καλλικέλαδον, καὶ λιγυραῖς μολπαῖς, κατακηλοῦσάν τε, καὶ ἀγλαΐζουσαν, τὴν Ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, εὔλαλον ἀηδόνα, δεῦτε εὐφημήσωμεν, Ἰωάννην τὸν πάνσοφον, τὸν Δαμασκηνὸν πιστοί, ὑμνογράφων τὸν πρύτανιν· τὸν ἔμπλεων, ἁπάσης γενόμενον, θείας καὶ κοσμικῆς σοφίας.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Τὴν ὡραιότητα — the first of the two apolytikia on the page of «Όσιος Ιωάννης ο Δαμασκηνός», and it names him.

english.text: Come, faithful, let us praise the sweet-singing and clear-voiced nightingale, who with melodious songs charms and adorns the Church of Christ — John the all-wise, the Damascene, the chief of the hymnographers, who became filled with all wisdom, divine and worldly.

hymns.text: Δαμάσας πολλοῖς, ἱδρῶσι τῆς ἀσκήσεως, τὸ σῶμα τὸ σόν, εἰς ὕψος οὐράνιον, εὐπετῶς ἀνέδραμες, ὅπου μέλη θεῖά σοι δίδονται, ἃ τρανῶς ἐμελῴδησας, τοῖς φίλοις Κυρίου Πάτερ Ὅσιε.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β’, Τὰ ἄνω ζητῶν — the kontakion on the page of «Όσιος Ιωάννης ο Δαμασκηνός». It plays on his name, Δαμάσας for Δαμασκηνός, and so names him.

english.text: Having subdued your body with many sweats of asceticism, you ran up lightly to the heavenly height, where divine songs are given you — those which you sang out plainly to the friends of the Lord, venerable father.

birth.note: saint.gr: «Γεννήθηκε στη Δαμασκό στα τέλη του 7ου αιώνα μ.Χ.». The page gives no year, only the end of that century. The Охридски пролог за 4. децембар ст. ст. gives no year of birth either, only an age at death — „у стотину четвртој години свога живота“, in the hundred and fourth year of his life — and that age is deliberately NOT subtracted from its year of death to make a birth year here.

death.note: **Two books twenty-seven years apart, and the interval holds both; it was a flat 749 before this reading.** saint.gr: «Έζησε με οσιότητα πάνω από εκατό χρόνια και κοιμήθηκε ειρηνικά το 749 μ.Χ.», and its heading for him reads «(; - 749)». The Охридски пролог за 4. децембар ст. ст. closes „Упокојио се мирно око 776. године у стотину четвртој години свога живота“ — he reposed in peace about 776 in the hundred and fourth year of his life. Both books make him over a hundred years old and they put his repose a generation apart; nothing is chosen and the basis stays traditional.
